title: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 3](/bible/leviticus/3)

**[Leviticus 3:1](/bible/leviticus/3#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/3#v1)</sup> And if his oblation be a sacrifice of peace offering, if he offer it of the herd; whether it be a male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before the Lord.

- The peace offering of the herd, whether male or female, must be offered without blemish before the Lord: no bruise, no cut, no stain, nothing superfluous like an extra member. Whatever the sacrifice is for the Lord, it has to be the best of the best, a flawless sacrifice.
- The Passover lamb shows how that was carried out. The lamb was without blemish, a male of the first year, taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut. It was kept up to the fourteenth day, isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself; and it was eaten roast with fire, not raw and not sodden with water, with the purtenance thereof, for after those days there was nothing left within it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 12:3-9](/bible/exodus/12#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/12#v3)</sup> Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/12#v4)</sup> And if the household be too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbour next unto his house take it according to the number of the souls; every man according to his eating shall make your count for the lamb.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/12#v5)</sup> Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats:
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/12#v6)</sup> And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/12#v7)</sup> And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/12#v8)</sup> And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/12#v9)</sup> Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.

    Your lamb shall be without blemish; it was taken out from the sheep, kept from the goats to the fourteenth day, and roasted with fire, not raw nor sodden.

- The lamb that had no blemish was symbolic of Christ. A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump: a little sin in the spirit will get worse, so the old leaven is purged out, and that is the true resemblance of the Passover, purging out sin not one day a year but constantly, in prayer and fasting; for even Christ our Passover, our lamb without blemish, is sacrificed for us.
- Christ gave himself for the church, that he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle, holy and without blemish, sanctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word.
- Christ did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: without blemish physically was symbolic of no sin. He was the one and only flawless sacrifice. He also suffered wrongfully, and that is thankworthy with God; when you follow his steps and suffer wrongfully without adding a blot to your honor, that is acceptable with God.
- John bore the record: behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. That goes back to presenting a glorious church; the only way to be without blemish is through faith in Christ.
- That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Corinthians 5:6-7](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v6)</sup> Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v7)</sup> Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us:

    A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump; purge out the old leaven, for even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.
  - **[Ephesians 5:25-27](/bible/ephesians/5#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/ephesians/5#v25)</sup> Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/ephesians/5#v26)</sup> That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word,
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/ephesians/5#v27)</sup> That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.

    Christ gave himself for the church, to present it a glorious church, holy and without blemish, as the Levitical sacrifices figured.
  - **[1 Peter 2:21-22](/bible/1-peter/2#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/1-peter/2#v21)</sup> For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/1-peter/2#v22)</sup> Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:

    Christ suffered for us, who did no sin; no blemish means no sin, the one flawless sacrifice.
  - **[1 Peter 2:19-20](/bible/1-peter/2#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/1-peter/2#v19)</sup> For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/1-peter/2#v20)</sup> For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.

    Enduring grief, suffering wrongfully, is thankworthy; that is what Christ went through for us, and the pattern for us when we suffer for well doing.
  - **[John 1:29](/bible/john/1#v29)**
    > <sup>[29](/bible/john/1#v29)</sup> The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

    Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ was that lamb.
  - **[Hebrews 10:1-4](/bible/hebrews/10#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/hebrews/10#v1)</sup> For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/hebrews/10#v2)</sup> For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/hebrews/10#v3)</sup> But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/hebrews/10#v4)</sup> For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.

    The law had a shadow of good things to come; the blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins, so Christ had to be the ultimate sacrifice.

**[Leviticus 3:2-16](/bible/leviticus/3#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/3#v2)</sup> And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and Aaron’s sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/3#v3)</sup> And he shall offer of the sacrifice of the peace offering an offering made by fire unto the Lord; the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/3#v4)</sup> And the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the flanks, and the caul above the liver, with the kidneys, it shall he take away.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/3#v5)</sup> And Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar upon the burnt sacrifice, which is upon the wood that is on the fire: it is an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/3#v6)</sup> And if his offering for a sacrifice of peace offering unto the Lord be of the flock; male or female, he shall offer it without blemish.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/3#v7)</sup> If he offer a lamb for his offering, then shall he offer it before the Lord.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/leviticus/3#v8)</sup> And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering, and kill it before the tabernacle of the congregation: and Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle the blood thereof round about upon the altar.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/leviticus/3#v9)</sup> And he shall offer of the sacrifice of the peace offering an offering made by fire unto the Lord; the fat thereof, and the whole rump, it shall he take off hard by the backbone; and the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/leviticus/3#v10)</sup> And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is by the flanks, and the caul above the liver, with the kidneys, it shall he take away.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/3#v11)</sup> And the priest shall burn it upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/3#v12)</sup> And if his offering be a goat, then he shall offer it before the Lord.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/3#v13)</sup> And he shall lay his hand upon the head of it, and kill it before the tabernacle of the congregation: and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle the blood thereof upon the altar round about.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/3#v14)</sup> And he shall offer thereof his offering, even an offering made by fire unto the Lord; the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/3#v15)</sup> And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is by the flanks, and the caul above the liver, with the kidneys, it shall he take away.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/3#v16)</sup> And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the Lord’s.

- The peace offering could be of the herd or of the flock, a lamb or a goat, male or female without blemish, unlike the burnt offering of chapter 1, which was a male. The offerer laid his hand upon the head of his offering and killed it at the door of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about.
- The blood, the fat that covers the inwards, the two kidneys with the fat upon them by the flanks, and the caul above the liver were the Lord's, burned upon the altar, the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour; the breast and the right shoulder were for the priest. All the fat is the Lord's.

**[Leviticus 3:17](/bible/leviticus/3#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/3#v17)</sup> It shall be a perpetual statute for your generations throughout all your dwellings, that ye eat neither fat nor blood.

- It shall be a perpetual statute that ye eat neither fat nor blood. This is a controversial scripture: brothers and sisters ask whether we are cut off for eating fat. Having that question is a good thing; it means you are reading to understand, not reading just to say you read four chapters.
- [Leviticus 7](/bible/leviticus/7) answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 7:22-25](/bible/leviticus/7#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/leviticus/7#v22)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/leviticus/7#v23)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat.
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/leviticus/7#v24)</sup> And the fat of the beast that dieth of itself, and the fat of that which is torn with beasts, may be used in any other use: but ye shall in no wise eat of it.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/leviticus/7#v25)</sup> For whosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord, even the soul that eateth it shall be cut off from his people.

    The fat forbidden is the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire; it belongs to the laws of sacrifice.
  - **[Romans 10:4](/bible/romans/10#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/romans/10#v4)</sup> For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

    Christ is the end of the law for righteousness; that goes into the sacrificial law.

- The blood was also for the altar of the Lord, but there is more to why the Lord had to say it. After Israel came out of Egypt, we had learned heathen practices there, such as drinking blood. The Lord said: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. Drinking the blood of animals was an Egyptian custom tied to their idols, and the blood-drinking customs of the Hamitic nations continue to this day.
- The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel and sanctified his people with these laws; these laws make us special, going back to [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and 6, how he separated us. Do not follow the customs and fashions of the heathen.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 7:26-27](/bible/leviticus/7#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/leviticus/7#v26)</sup> Moreover ye shall eat no manner of blood, whether it be of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings.
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/leviticus/7#v27)</sup> Whatsoever soul it be that eateth any manner of blood, even that soul shall be cut off from his people.

    Ye shall eat no manner of blood; whatsoever soul eateth any manner of blood shall be cut off from his people.
  - **[Leviticus 18:1-3](/bible/leviticus/18#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/18#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/18#v2)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, I am the Lord your God.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/18#v3)</sup> After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.

    After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Israel had to be commanded away from what was learned there.
  - **[Exodus 11:7](/bible/exodus/11#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/11#v7)</sup> But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.

    The Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; his laws sanctify his people.
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:6](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6)</sup> For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

    Thou art an holy people chosen to be a special people; the dietary laws are part of that separation.

- Israel fell into this sin in Saul's day: the people flew upon the spoil and ate with the blood, and Saul said, ye have transgressed. Eating with the blood is sin; that is why you make sure your food is thoroughly cooked, well done, cut open to the bone so it cooks through. Meat served rare is not running with juice, it is blood.
- Serve the Lord and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, and take sickness away from the midst of thee: keep the dietary laws, what to eat and not eat, how to cook it and how to season it, and do not bow down to the gods of the heathen nor do after their works.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Samuel 14:33-34](/bible/1-samuel/14#v33)**
    > <sup>[33](/bible/1-samuel/14#v33)</sup> Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
    >
    > <sup>[34](/bible/1-samuel/14#v34)</sup> And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.

    The people sinned against the Lord in eating with the blood; Saul had every man slay his beast on the great stone so they sinned not.
  - **[Exodus 23:23-25](/bible/exodus/23#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/exodus/23#v23)</sup> For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/exodus/23#v24)</sup> Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/exodus/23#v25)</sup> And ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.

    Do not do after the works of the heathen; serve the Lord, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water and take sickness away from the midst of thee.
